research_question: What is the effect of estrogen-alone therapy (oral, transdermal, or vaginal estradiol or conjugated estrogens, at any dose), compared with placebo or no treatment, on overall sexual function in perimenopausal and postmenopausal women?
treatment_label: Estrogen alone (oral, transdermal or vaginal estradiol / conjugated estrogens, any dose)
outcome_description: A single composite or overall sexual function score per trial at the end of treatment, extracted as mean, SD and n per arm. Preference order: validated overall sexual function instruments (e.g. Female Sexual Function Index total/full score, McCoy Female Sexuality Questionnaire total); otherwise the sexual domain or sexual item of a broader menopause/quality-of-life instrument (e.g. MENQoL sexual domain, Women's Health Questionnaire sexual functioning subscale). All scales oriented so that a higher value indicates better sexual function; bother/symptom-severity scales (e.g. MENQoL sexual domain) are sign-reversed before analysis. End-of-treatment values preferred; mean change from baseline with SD of change used for both arms if only change data are reported (recorded as change scores). SE/SEM converted to SD = SE x sqrt(n). If multiple within-treatment time points are reported, the last time point at or before end of treatment is used. In multi-arm trials, only estrogen-alone arms (doses combined: pooled means and SDs, summed n) and the placebo arm are included; estrogen+progestogen or estrogen+testosterone arms are ignored.
positive_direction: A positive Hedges' g means better sexual function with estrogen-alone therapy than with placebo or no treatment (favours estrogen).
search_queries: estrogen therapy sexual function postmenopausal women randomized placebo-controlled trial
estradiol conjugated estrogens Female Sexual Function Index trial menopause

inclusion_criteria: Randomised trial comparing estrogen alone (any route, any dose) with placebo or no treatment in perimenopausal or postmenopausal women

Reports some quantitative measure of sexual function (overall score, composite score, or sexual domain/item of a broader menopause or quality-of-life instrument) during or at the end of the treatment period
Reports data sufficient to compute an effect size (means and SDs/SEs per arm, or statistics convertible to them)
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic review, meta-analysis, narrative review, editorial, opinion piece, theoretical/modelling paper, protocol or conference abstract without data)

No comparison between an estrogen-alone treatment arm and a placebo or no-treatment control arm (e.g. control receives another hormone, progestogen, testosterone, DHEA, tibolone or a vaginal moisturizer; single-arm or head-to-head hormone comparisons only)
No quantitative outcome data from which an effect size can be computed (no means+SDs, SEs, t/F values, proportions or odds ratios)

Completely unrelated to the research topic (e.g. premenopausal women only, women treated for cancer, or only vasomotor, vaginal atrophy, bone, endometrial or adverse-effect outcomes, or sexual function measured only after treatment cessation)
moderators_to_extract: Route of estrogen administration (oral, transdermal, vaginal)
Estrogen type and dose (estradiol vs conjugated estrogens; low vs standard dose)
Menopausal status of sample (perimenopausal, postmenopausal, mixed) and mean age
Sexual function instrument used (FSFI total, McCoy MFSQ, MENQoL sexual domain, WHQ, other)
Outcome data type (end-of-treatment value vs change from baseline) and sample size category
effect_size_note: Pool with a random-effects model (DerSimonian-Laird or REML) using Hedges' g standardised mean difference computed from end-of-treatment means, SDs and n per arm. Convert SE/SEM to SD (SD = SE x sqrt(n)); reverse the sign of bother/severity-oriented scales so higher = better sexual function; combine multiple estrogen dose arms into one group before computing the effect size. One sexual function measure per trial.
